titular: US inflation triggers $723m in crypto liquidations
resum: After the US inflation data, bitcoin fell almost 2% to around $73,700, and $723m in bets from more than 115,000 traders were liquidated in 24 hours, most of them betting on rises.
per_que_importa: A liquidation means that someone who bet with borrowed money (leverage) loses their position all at once when the price moves against them. With leverage, a small drop can wipe out everything you put in.

titular: Binance thieves still control more than $3bn
resum: According to analytics firm Elliptic, about $3.13bn of the $6.3bn stolen from Binance remains in the attackers' wallets, mostly in bitcoin and ether, which nobody can freeze. The hackers, believed to be North Korean, have created at least six 'meme' coins to launder part of it.
per_que_importa: When crypto is stolen there is no guarantee fund like the one for bank deposits: getting it back depends on freezing it in time, and that is only possible with some types of coin.

titular: Initia network hit by its second attack in under three weeks
resum: Hackers stole about $3.27m from the Initia blockchain after obtaining an access key to its Google cloud and GitHub accounts. The network has been halted and about $2.16m has been frozen; the first attack, on 23 October, cost $2.7m.
per_que_importa: Many attacks don't break the blockchain technology itself but the IT systems of the company behind it: a platform's security depends on how people run it.

titular: Santander, BBVA and 19 other banks put $270m into a shared stablecoin
resum: A consortium of 21 institutions, including Citi, Goldman Sachs, Santander, BBVA, Deutsche Bank and BNP Paribas, has committed about $270m to Project Faro, a dollar-pegged stablecoin planned for the first half of 2027, with a euro version to follow. So far, confirmed details are thin.
per_que_importa: Stablecoins aim to move digital money quickly and cheaply; big banks getting involved, including two Spanish ones, could bring the technology to everyday payments under banking regulation.

titular: US bitcoin funds lose $1.5bn in a week
resum: US exchange-traded bitcoin funds have seen outflows of about $1.5bn since 2 November, and BlackRock's fund has had seven straight sessions of redemptions. Miner MARA has also sold 13,597 bitcoins (about $1.1bn) in six weeks.
per_que_importa: When big investors and companies sell at the same time, the price can fall fast. It's a reminder that bitcoin is a highly volatile asset with no guaranteed value.

titular: US market regulator brings fewest enforcement actions since 1991
resum: The SEC brought 348 enforcement actions in fiscal year 2026, almost 24% fewer than the year before and the lowest number since 1991. Civil penalties totalled $343m; crypto cases included fake platforms that defrauded small investors.
per_que_importa: Less oversight means that if something goes wrong, it's less likely anyone will be held responsible. That's why it's key to check that a platform is registered before trusting it with money.

titular: Deutsche Bank starts holding crypto for clients in Europe
resum: The German bank is offering custody of bitcoin, ether and three stablecoins (USDC, EURC and EURAU) to companies and institutional investors, not individuals. It does so under the EU MiCA licence it obtained on 12 October and plans to expand to Asia in 2027.
per_que_importa: The EU's MiCA rules allow regulated banks into this business. That offers stronger custody safeguards, but doesn't remove the risk of a cryptocurrency's price falling.
